raw:
You leave the exchange alone, keeping your attention on the roast.

The demon woman in the archway shifts her splinted wrist closer to her side. “I know. We’ve got cards out. You said right after dinner.”

Rashid’s hand stills beside his plate. “Dena, I said I’d be there.”

“Not after a drill.”

He glances toward Ashara. “Ashara asked for half an hour at the octagon.”

Ashara sets down her fork. “You had another arrangement?”

“An earlier one.”

“Then you should’ve said no to one of them.”

Dena’s expression tightens. “Don’t make me arbitrate it. I came because you hadn’t told us.”

For a moment Rashid looks at neither of them. Then he nods once. “You’re right. I said cards first. I’ll be there when I’m done eating.”

Ashara leans back in her chair. Her tail taps once against the wood. “Fine. I’ll find another partner.”

“Your bout is tomorrow,” Rashid says.

“And Dena’s evening is tonight.”

Dena exhales through her nose, some of the edge leaving her face. “It’s cards, Rashid. Not a tribunal. Eat before the potatoes congeal, then come lose at something.”

“I don’t play for money.”

“That’s what you say before you lose.”

One of the students behind her snorts. Dena turns and heads back toward the common room, the others following; the soft, papery shuffle of cards begins again beyond the arch.

Ashara takes another bite of roast. “You make a very elaborate hobby of making your own life difficult.”

Rashid’s smile is brief. “I’m told I have range.”

Seraphel tears her bread in half.

“Eat while it is warm.  
Regret keeps poorly.”

Caelindra has been watching the exchange with an expression that gives nothing away. She finally looks back to you.

“You had access to a Fae library,” she says. “What was the least boring thing you copied?”
